name: Derivative suits

subjectOf.text: Germany's 2005 introduction of the derivative suit tightened the standard of care only partially, because section 148(1) of the AktG conditions shareholder standing on holding shares worth roughly 100,000 euros, a threshold with no U.S. counterpart.
subjectOf.abstract: section 148(1) of the AktG requires a threshold ownership of shares totaling !100,000 (about $127,090) for shareholders to have standing to sue on behalf 174 of the corporation in German courts
subjectOf.citation: Painter and Kaal, Initial Reflections on an Evolving Standard Constraints on Risk Taking by Directors and Officers in (2010). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1558614
scope_conditions: German derivative suits under section 148(1) AktG as amended by the UMAG
partly counterbalanced by VorstAG liability and compensation reduction provisions

subjectOf.text: Because CIAs combine contractual and public enforcement, with the OIG enforcing them and private rights of action also available, they are more than contractual arrangements, and a breach of a CIA may be treated like a breach of law for purposes of the duty of care.
subjectOf.abstract: Because of the combination of enforcement mechanisms, CIAs are more than contractual arrangements. A breach of a CIA may be treated like a breach of law for purposes of the duty of care.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580
scope_conditions: CIAs enforceable by the OIG and, under Delaware law, by courts via derivative suit

subjectOf.text: Courts treat companies that executed a CIA differently from other companies, and are increasingly recognizing the role of CIAs and their implications for directors' fiduciary duties.
subjectOf.abstract: Courts, however, treat companies that executed a CIA differently. Courts are increasingly recognizing the role of CIAs and their implications for directors' fiduciary duties.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580
scope_conditions: derivative litigation involving companies operating under a CIA
